patterns.comment: table row: any line carrying a divider with no colon before it, claimed before the line rules below because a row's first cell now opens the line rather than sitting behind a border. A colon before the first pipe makes a 'name: value' line whose value holds the pipe, which the line rules below colour — unless the line is capitalised: 'Currency: EUR|symbol' is a table's header, its first cell the Concept and the default it states. An '=' inside a word ('a=b') is a letter of the cell; only a space-preceded one opens Python (a Concept's derivation in the first header cell). The pipes (and any stray dashes/crosses) share the separator's quiet chrome colour so all table symbols read alike, upright; cell text falls to cell-safe shapes and the extension's semantic tokens overlay the parsed truth (attribute / Example / value / formula)
a header whose first cell states the Concept's default: 'Currency: EUR|symbol'
a table whose Python wrote it: the Concept and its derivation in the first header cell
a first cell not starting with a lowercase letter: a capital, a number ('1. Trip', '3D Print') or a script with no capitals ('日本語')
a script with no capitals has no case to tell the two apart, so the shape does: a term with a colon is an attribute's ('名前: 太郎')

Concept at the start of a line, in any alphabet: a number ('1. Trip', '3D Print') or a script with no capitals ('日本語') opens one as a capital does. Anything else a line can open with has a rule of its own below

Concept: a type / class, the structural backbone. A quote ends the name, but an apostrophe inside a word is a letter of it — 'Aristotle's Ethics' is one name, so a ' followed by a letter is consumed rather than closing the run. A derivation ends it too: in 'Sales =by_month(@raw)' the Concept is 'Sales' and the rest is the Python that writes its table
patterns.name: entity.name.type.concept.aot

patterns.comment: derivation on a line with no value: a Concept's Python ('Sales =by_month(@raw)'), claimed whole so none of its names reads as a Concept or an attribute. A value's derivation stands after its colon and is coloured with the value; the extension's semantic tokens tell formula from Python on both
patterns.name: meta.embedded.inline.python.aot

patterns.comment: value: the data after a colon. A run of '=' at its start or after a space is the escape for a literal '=' ('a == b' reads 'a = b'), shown as one; a lone space-preceded '=' opens the value's derivation, which the extension's semantic tokens paint as Python over this
patterns.name: string.unquoted.value.aot

patterns.comment: literal: verbatim / raw text in backticks
patterns.name: markup.inline.raw.literal.aot
